name: godot-mcp-runtime

tools.name: launch_editor
tools.description: Open the Godot editor GUI for a project, for the human user. Use only when the user asks to open the editor; for agent-driven work use the headless scene and node tools (add_node, set_node_properties, etc.), since the editor cannot be controlled programmatically. Returns: projectPath, the editor process pid and message. Errors if projectPath has no project.godot or the editor process does not start.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

tools.name: run_project
tools.description: Start a runtime session: spawn the project (stdout/stderr captured; asks the user to confirm the first time per project), or with attach: true wait for a Godot you launch yourself (nothing spawned or captured). Required before take_screenshot, simulate_input, get_ui_elements and run_script; returns once the bridge answers. It becomes current; others keep running. Returns: projectPath, sessionMode, bridgePort, message; warnings leads on a start caveat. Errors if the bridge never answers.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

attach.description: If true, do not spawn Godot: inject the bridge and wait for a Godot process you launch yourself (up to 20s for it to start listening, 45s total once it has). Call before Godot launches, or start the launch in parallel, because Godot reads autoloads only at startup. One attach session per project; attaching again keeps this server's attached session unless its bridge is gone, and says so in warnings. Cannot be combined with scene, background or profiling. Nothing is captured: get_debug_output returns null logs with a warning, and the profiler is unavailable.

scene.description: Scene to run (path relative to project, e.g. "scenes/main.tscn"). Omit to use the project's main scene. Not valid with attach: true. Must end in .tscn, .scn, .escn, .tres or .res.

background.description: If true, the game window is never shown on Windows and is moved off-screen after startup on other platforms; mouse input passes through to whatever is beneath it. Programmatic input (simulate_input, run_script) and screenshots stay fully active. It does not guarantee the game never takes keyboard focus. Not valid with attach: true.

bridgePort.description: TCP port for the MCP bridge. Omit to auto-select a free port (recommended). Spawned sessions receive it through an environment variable; attach mode bakes it into the injected bridge script, so the Godot you launch listens on exactly this port. A port held by a live session on another project is refused.

profiling.description: Attach Godot's own remote debugger so profile_project, start_profiler and stop_profiler can measure this session. Must be set at launch - a session already running cannot be profiled - and costs a little runtime overhead. Not valid with attach: true.

tools.name: switch_project
tools.description: Point the runtime tools (screenshots, input, UI, run_script, debug output, profiling, stop_project) at another project's session. Needed only when several sessions exist; run_project makes its own session current. A session whose game exited can be selected to read its logs or stop it: live is then false and warnings leads. Returns: projectPath, previousProjectPath, live, sessionMode, bridgePort, bridgeResponsive, message. Errors if the project has no session, listing the live ones.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory whose session becomes the current one. check_project lists the live sessions.

tools.name: get_debug_output
tools.description: Read captured stdout/stderr from a spawned Godot project. Use whenever a runtime tool fails unexpectedly: script errors, missing nodes and crash backtraces surface here. Still works after the process exits or crashes; the logs are kept until stop_project. Returns: projectPath, sessionMode, output and errors (last `limit` lines each, default 200), running (false after exit) and exitCode after exit. An attached session captures nothing: output, errors and running are null and warnings leads.

limit.description: Max lines to return, a whole number of 1 or more (default: 200, from end of output)

tools.name: stop_project
tools.description: End the current session now and remove the bridge, cutting off a runtime call in progress. A spawned Godot is stopped; an attached one is detached, not killed. Other sessions keep running; none becomes current. Also frees a spawned game that exited by itself (alreadyExited). Returns: projectPath, message, sessionMode, externalProcessPreserved, alreadyExited, exitCode, killUnconfirmed, finalOutput, finalErrors; warnings leads if the kill or cleanup was unconfirmed. Errors if nothing is running.

tools.name: take_screenshot
tools.description: Save a PNG of the running viewport under .mcp/godot-runtime/screenshots/ (kept after stop_project). responseMode: preview (default; inline, fits default 960x540, max 1920x1080), full (inline PNG, for small text), path_only (no image). Returns: projectPath, path, size, stats {chromatic, dominant, distinct, likelyBlank} from the full PNG, so a blank frame shows without vision. warnings leads if stats is null or the image is too big to inline. Errors: no session, no frame rendered, bridge timeout.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds to wait for the screenshot, a whole number from 1 to 600000 (default: 10000); a value from 59001 to 60000 is refused, since the answer would not fit a client's 60s request timeout. Time spent waiting for the session queue comes off it, and a call left with under 2000 ms is refused with nothing sent. The game gives up on a frame that never renders after 5000 ms and reports that; a lower timeout expires first.

responseMode.description: Response payload mode. "preview" returns a bounded inline preview plus paths (default). "full" returns the full inline PNG. "path_only" returns paths only. An image file over 3 MiB, or a full PNG that could not be decoded, is not inlined: the path is returned with a leading warning.

previewMaxWidth.description: Width in pixels of the box the preview is fitted into when responseMode is "preview". Default: 960. Maximum: 1920; a larger value is clamped to it, not refused. Use responseMode "full" for the screenshot at its own size.

previewMaxHeight.description: Height in pixels of the box the preview is fitted into when responseMode is "preview". Default: 540. Maximum: 1080; a larger value is clamped to it, not refused.

tools.name: simulate_input
tools.description: Send input actions. key, mouse_button, action: omit `pressed` to tap; set it to hold or release. click_element takes a node path or name (see get_ui_elements), not text, and scrolls its target into view. Returns: projectPath, success, results[]: ok, hit, scrolled, signals, `changes`, `watch`, mouse_motion `position` (as delivered), `errors` (spawned only); warnings leads if `errors` is partial. An invalid batch injects nothing; a failure skips the rest. A covered or clipped click is refused.

actions.description: Array of input actions to execute sequentially. Each object must have a "type" field. A batch whose time budget (waits, holds, and every frame counted at 10fps) exceeds 600s is rejected before anything is injected: split it across calls. The budget admits at most 5900 actions per call, fewer when they tap, hold or wait. When results outgrow one reply (about 4 MiB), later entries keep only index, type, ok, frame, elapsed_ms and error, with details_dropped: true; the action still ran.

key.description: [key] Godot KEY_* constant name without the prefix (e.g. "W", "Space", "Escape", "Enter", "Tab", "Up", "PageUp"). Errors on unrecognized names.

pressed.description: [key, mouse_button, action] Omit to tap: the action presses, holds briefly, and releases by itself. Set true to press and hold across later actions (reported in still_held), false to release an earlier hold. Cannot be combined with hold_ms.

hold_ms.description: [key, mouse_button, action] Tap hold duration in milliseconds, overriding the default (one process frame plus one physics frame for key/action, zero gap for mouse_button). Use it for code polling is_action_pressed over real time. Rejected when pressed is also set. Max 10000.

unicode.description: [key] Unicode codepoint for text-entry Controls (LineEdit, TextEdit). Auto-derived for ASCII letters/digits (respecting shift); pass explicitly for symbols or non-ASCII. E.g. 33 for "!", 64 for "@".

x.description: [mouse_button, mouse_motion] X position in viewport pixels (0,0 = top-left), as get_ui_elements reports them; a stretch mode is converted

y.description: [mouse_button, mouse_motion] Y position in viewport pixels (0,0 = top-left), as get_ui_elements reports them; a stretch mode is converted

element.description: [click_element] Identifies the UI element to click. Accepts: absolute node path (e.g. "/root/HUD/Button"), relative node path, or node name (BFS matched). Use get_ui_elements to discover valid names and paths.

action.description: [action] Godot input action name (as defined in Project Settings > Input Map). Sent as an InputEventAction: input handlers see it like its bound key, and ui_* actions act on the focused Control (ui_text_* editing actions do not; use key or text).

text.description: [text] String to type into whatever Control currently holds focus, expanded to one key press+release per character. Fails when nothing holds focus - click or focus the LineEdit first. Max 1000 characters.

ms.description: [wait] Real-time pause in milliseconds, for time-driven things such as cooldowns and animations (~16ms = one frame at 60fps). Exactly one of ms or frames is required. Counts toward the batch's 600s time budget, and a batch whose total wait approaches 60s may be cut off by your client before the server answers: split it across calls.

frames.description: [wait] Deterministic pause of N engine process frames, for stepping game logic rather than waiting on the clock. Exactly one of ms or frames is required. Max 600, budgeted at a 10fps floor, so a wait of several hundred frames may be cut off by your client before the server answers.

watch.description: Godot NodePath:property strings sampled after every action and reported per result, e.g. "/root/Main/Player:position". Property subnames are allowed ("/root/Main/Player:position:x"). Read-only; an unresolvable path samples as null instead of failing the batch.

tools.name: get_ui_elements
tools.description: List the running scene Controls with rect, type and text. Call before simulate_input click_element to find names and paths. Needs a runtime session. visibleOnly (default true) drops hidden Controls and ones clipped out of view. filter narrows by class; root limits the list to one Control and its descendants. Returns: projectPath, elements[] with path/type/rect/visible/onScreen (visibleRect if clipped), optional text/disabled/tooltip. Errors on a non-Control filter or an unknown root.

visibleOnly.description: Only return Controls that are visible in the tree and have area on screen, not clipped away by a ScrollContainer, a clip_contents ancestor or the viewport (default: true). Set false to include the rest.

filter.description: Filter by native Control class name (e.g. "Button", "Label", "LineEdit"); subclasses match. A class Control inherits from (CanvasItem, Node) lists every Control. Any other name, including a script class_name, is an error.

root.description: List only this Control and its descendants. Same lookup as simulate_input click_element: absolute path, relative path or node name (BFS matched). Visibility and clipping by ancestors above it still apply. An unknown name, or a node that is not a Control, is an error.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run GDScript in the running game. It must extend RefCounted and define func execute(scene_tree: SceneTree) -> Variant; execute may await, cut off at the timeout (not cancelled). Return is JSON-serialized: vectors as {x,y[,z,w]}, Color as {r,g,b,a}, a Node as {class,name,path}. Compiled with project warnings. Returns: projectPath, result, warnings, tip. Spawned: a runtime error is an error if result is null, else a warning. Attached: errors are unobservable. Asks the user once per project.

script.description: GDScript source code. Must contain "extends RefCounted" and "func execute(scene_tree: SceneTree) -> Variant".

timeout.description: Timeout in ms, a whole number from 1 to 600000 (default: 30000); a value from 59001 to 60000 is refused, since the answer would not fit a client's 60s request timeout. Increase for long-running scripts. Time spent on the confirmation prompt and waiting for the session queue comes off it; a call left with under 2000 ms is refused with nothing sent.

tools.name: render_movie
tools.description: Render `frames` frames of the project (or `scene`) in a separate movie-writer run: no bridge, session or input (to interact: run_project, simulate_input). mode check (default): stats, likelyBlank, motion, inline frames, files deleted. frames: keeps PNGs. video: .avi/.ogv, no stats. Returns: frameCount, likelyBlank, anyMotion, samples, paths, bytesWritten; warnings leads if unmeasured or unconfirmed. Needs a display; asks the user once per project. Errors on timeout, failed run or live session.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scene.description: Scene to render (path relative to project, e.g. "scenes/main.tscn"). Omit to use the project's main scene. Must end in .tscn, .scn, .escn, .tres or .res.

mode.description: "check" (default) measures a sample of frames, returns a few inline, and deletes every file. "frames" keeps the PNG sequence (and frame.wav) under .mcp/godot-runtime/movies/ and returns paths plus stats for a sample. "video" writes one movie file and returns its path; it has no pixel stats.

frames.description: Frames to render before Godot quits (default 30, max 600). The first frames can be blank while the scene loads; likelyBlank is judged on the last one. The run is budgeted at 30s plus 250ms per frame, and a run that overruns it takes up to 10s more to stop. A run of 77 to 80 frames is refused, with nothing run, because its answer would not fit a client's 60s request timeout; above that a client may cut the call off before this server can report a timeout.

fps.description: Fixed simulation and capture rate (default 30, max 120). Game time covered is frames / fps seconds, whatever the wall-clock speed.

inlineFrames.description: [check] Inline images to return, evenly spaced and ending at the last frame (default 3, max 6; 0 for none). Each is downscaled to fit 960x540; stats are measured at full size. Rejected in other modes.

format.description: [video] Movie container (default "avi"). "ogv" needs an engine that can write it; the error names the format and engine version when it cannot. Rejected in other modes.

tools.name: list_autoloads
tools.description: List the autoloads registered in a project, with their paths and singleton flags. Use first when diagnosing headless failures: an autoload that stops the engine before an operation is dispatched fails every headless operation. Reads project.godot directly, no Godot process. Returns: autoloads[], each { name, path, singleton }, one per name (the last assignment, which the engine keeps); empty when none. warnings leads when a line is not listed or is not in the form Godot writes.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

tools.name: add_autoload
tools.description: Register a new autoload. autoloadPath takes res://... or a project path. singleton defaults to true. No Godot process is used. An autoload that stops the engine before a headless operation is dispatched fails all of them: run validate on it first. Returns: autoload { name, path, singleton } read back from project.godot, and a tip. Errors if the name exists (use update_autoload), or a singleton shares its name with a class_name a project script declares (the engine then drops the script).

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

autoloadPath.description: Path to the script or scene (e.g. "res://autoload/my_manager.gd" or "autoload/my_manager.gd")

singleton.description: Register as a globally accessible singleton by name (default: true)

tools.name: remove_autoload
tools.description: Unregister an autoload from a project by name. Use to recover from an autoload that stops the engine before headless operations are dispatched. No Godot process is used. Returns: removed (the name) and autoloads[], the entries that remain, read back from project.godot. Errors if no autoload has that name.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

autoloadName.description: Name of the autoload to remove

tools.name: update_autoload
tools.description: Change an existing autoload's path or singleton flag. Pass autoloadPath, singleton or both; errors if neither is given. An omitted field keeps its current value. Use instead of remove_autoload plus add_autoload: one edit, no window where the autoload is missing. No Godot process is used. Returns: autoload { name, path, singleton } read back from project.godot. Errors if autoloadName is not registered, or if the result is a singleton named like a class_name a project script declares.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

autoloadName.description: Name of the autoload to update

autoloadPath.description: New path to the script or scene

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Find Godot projects under a directory by locating project.godot files. Use when no project is named; to inspect a known one use check_project. recursive: true descends into subdirectories (skipping .git, .godot, node_modules, etc.); the default checks the directory and its immediate children. Returns: projects[], each { projectPath, name }, name being config/name else the folder name. warnings leads when a path could not be read or a link was not followed. Errors if directory is not a directory.

directory.description: Directory to search for Godot projects

tools.name: check_project
tools.description: Get project metadata and the Godot version, plus a runtime block. runtime.activeSession, sessionMode and bridgeResponsive describe the current session, projectPath its project (null when none), liveSessions all live ones. With projectPath, runtime.project is that project's session: live, exited or none. Returns: { name?, projectPath?, structure?, godotVersion, runtime }; warnings leads if structure is partial or the engine is newer than the project. Errors if projectPath lacks project.godot.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory (optional - omit to get Godot version and runtime status only). An empty string is treated as omitted.

tools.name: get_project_files
tools.description: Return the file tree of a Godot project. Use to discover project structure when paths are unknown. subfolder lists one folder as the root (maxDepth counts from it). extensions filters files (e.g. ["gd","tscn"]) and drops directories with no match; maxDepth -1 is unlimited. Skips dot-prefixed entries. Returns: the root node { name, type, path, children[] }; a child is a file, a directory, or a link (not followed). A directory not opened or unreadable has children null; warnings leads then.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

subfolder.description: Folder inside the project to list instead of the whole project (e.g. "ui/themes" or "res://ui"). Must exist and be a directory. Omit for the project root.

maxDepth.description: Maximum recursion depth, counted from the listed root. -1 means unlimited (default: -1)

extensions.description: Filter to only these file extensions (e.g. ["gd", "tscn"]); directories with no match are left out. Omit to include all.

tools.name: search_project
tools.description: Plain-text (substring, not regex) search across project files; the text goes in `pattern`. Default fileTypes ["gd","tscn","cs","gdshader"]; caseSensitive false; maxResults integer >= 1, default 100. Skips hidden entries and .mcp. Returns: matches[] (project-relative file, 1-indexed lineNumber, line), truncated, filesSearched, fileTypes. warnings leads when no file had a searched extension or a path was unreadable. Errors if pattern holds a line break or a parameter is undeclared.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

pattern.description: Plain-text string to search for (required; there is no query or regex parameter)

maxResults.description: Maximum matches to return, an integer of 1 or more (default: 100)

tools.name: get_scene_dependencies
tools.description: Parse a .tscn file for ext_resource references (scripts, textures, subscenes). Use to see what a scene depends on before refactoring or moving files. Returns: scenePath and dependencies[], one per ext_resource reference (path, type, optional uid). warnings leads when ext_resource lines could not be read. Errors if the file does not exist or is not a text scene or resource.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Path to the .tscn file relative to the project root (e.g. "scenes/main.tscn")

tools.name: get_project_settings
tools.description: Parse project.godot into JSON without launching Godot. Use to inspect display, input and rendering settings. Pass section for one INI section. Returns: settings as { [section]: { [key]: value } }, or { [key]: value } plus section. Strings are unescaped, an empty value is null, complex values stay raw text. Keys before any section are under __global__. warnings leads when the section is absent, a value is unterminated or empty, a line is not as Godot writes it, or a setting is assigned twice.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

section.description: Filter to a specific INI section (e.g. "display", "application"). Omit for all sections; an empty string is treated as omitted.

tools.name: set_project_setting
tools.description: Set one project.godot setting without launching Godot. Pass value (JSON, converted to a Godot literal) or literal (raw Godot text, e.g. "Vector2i(1280, 720)"), not both. Rewrites the last assignment in place or adds key/section; other lines stay byte for byte. Refuses autoload/* (use the autoload tools). Returns: { section, key, value read back, created, sectionCreated, previous? }.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

section.description: INI section, e.g. "display" or "application". Letters, digits and _ . - /, no spaces.

key.description: Setting key within the section, e.g. "window/size/viewport_width". Same character set as section.

value.description: JSON value converted to a Godot literal: a string is quoted, an integer-valued number is an int (write 2 as literal "2.0" for a float), a boolean is true/false, an array becomes [a, b], an object a dictionary. null is not accepted; use literal "null".

literal.description: Raw Godot literal written as is, on one line, with no trailing comment: "str", 1.5, true, null, [1, 2], {"a": 1} or a constructor such as Vector2i(1, 2) or PackedStringArray("a"). Checked by reading it back as one complete value. Resource(...), Object(...), ExtResource(...) and SubResource(...) are refused: Godot may then fail to load project.godot.

tools.name: create_scene
tools.description: Create a new scene file with a single root node, written to scenePath. Use to start a scene from scratch; to add nodes to an existing scene use add_node. rootNodeType defaults to Node2D: pass "Node3D" for 3D or "Control" for UI. Saves automatically and overwrites an existing file silently. Returns: the scenePath that was written. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project (e.g. "scenes/main.tscn")

tools.name: add_node
tools.description: Add a node to a scene, or instance another scene when nodeType is a scene path. Saves automatically. Values in properties are checked against each property's declared type; a mismatch errors (Property Values in docs/tools.md). Returns: nodeName, nodeType and nodePath, read back after the add; warnings leads when Godot renamed the node or a value will not be saved. Errors and adds nothing if the type, parent or a property is invalid. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

nodeType.description: Godot node class to instantiate (e.g. "Sprite2D", "CollisionShape2D", "Label"), or a project-relative scene path (.tscn or .scn, e.g. "scenes/enemy.tscn") to instance an existing scene as a child - instanced children serialize as `instance=ExtResource(...)` on save

nodeName.description: Name for the new node as it appears in the scene tree

parentNodePath.description: Parent node path from scene root (e.g. "root/Player"). Defaults to the root node; an empty string also means the root.

position.description: Position: {"x": 100, "y": 200} on a 2D node, {"x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 0} on a 3D node. Shorthand for properties.position; properties wins on a conflict.

rotation.description: Rotation in radians, for a 2D node. On a 3D node rotation is a vector: pass it as properties.rotation, {"x", "y", "z"} in radians. Shorthand for properties.rotation; properties wins on a conflict.

scale.description: Scale: {"x": 2, "y": 2} on a 2D node, {"x": 2, "y": 2, "z": 2} on a 3D node. Shorthand for properties.scale; properties wins on a conflict.

visible.description: Whether the node is visible. Shorthand for properties.visible; properties wins on a conflict.

modulate.description: Color modulation (e.g. {"r": 1, "g": 0, "b": 0, "a": 1}). Shorthand for properties.modulate; properties wins on a conflict.

properties.description: Additional property values as a JSON object. A key here wins over the same top-level shorthand (position, rotation, scale, visible, modulate). An Object-typed property takes a res:// path, a {type: ClassName, ...props} dict that builds a Resource inline, or null; slash-suffixed keys like shader_parameter/<uniform> go inside that dict, not on the node; metadata/<name> and slash keys the node declares go straight into properties. Coercion and Packed*Array / Array[T] / Dictionary[K, V] element rules: Property Values in docs/tools.md.

tools.name: load_sprite
tools.description: Set the texture on an existing Sprite2D, Sprite3D or TextureRect. For a new node, pass texture in add_node properties instead. Saves automatically. texturePath must be a file under projectPath. Returns: nodePath, nodeType and texturePath, read back from the node after the assignment. Errors if the node is not one of those three classes or the texture file does not exist. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

nodePath.description: Path to the target node from scene root (e.g. "root/Player/Sprite2D")

texturePath.description: Path to the texture file relative to the project (e.g. "assets/player.png")

tools.name: save_scene
tools.description: Re-pack and save a scene, optionally to another path (save-as). The mutation tools save by themselves: use this only for save-as via newPath, or to re-canonicalize a hand-edited .tscn. Overwrites silently. A newPath file gets no uid of its own. Returns: scenePath (loaded) and savedScenePath (written, confirmed on disk); warnings leads if the save dropped content. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

newPath.description: Save to a different path (relative to project) instead of overwriting the original

tools.name: export_mesh_library
tools.description: Export a scene's MeshInstance3D children as a MeshLibrary for GridMap. The outputPath extension sets the format: .tres is text (prefer it: readable, diffable), .res is binary. Not for 2D scenes. meshItemNames picks a subset, else all. Overwrites silently. Returns: outputPath, itemCount, itemNames read from the saved library; warnings leads when a requested name was not exported. Errors if no valid meshes, or while a runtime session is live.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

outputPath.description: Output path for the MeshLibrary (relative to project). Its extension sets the format: .tres writes text, .res writes binary. Prefer .tres.

meshItemNames.description: Names of specific mesh items to export. Omit to export all.

tools.name: batch_scene_operations
tools.description: Run several scene mutations in one process; every mutated scene is saved at the end. Use instead of chaining add_node, load_sprite, set_node_properties or save_scene. Each item sets operation (save stands for save_scene) and takes that tool's params. abortOnError stops at the first failure; later items return skipped: true. Returns: results[] in input order: operation, scenePath, success, error or skipped, plus the operation's own fields. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

operations.description: Ordered list of scene operations. Each item has its own operation and scenePath.

scenePath.description: Scene file path for this operation

updates.description: [set_node_properties] Property updates to apply in this operation

value.description: New value. Vector2/Vector3/Color auto-convert from {"x","y"} / {"x","y","z"} / {"r","g","b","a"} objects; primitives pass through. For Packed*Array properties, a plain array applies the same conversions element-wise (e.g. [{"x":10,"y":20}, ...] for Polygon2D.polygon); an element that cannot represent the packed element type errors instead of silently storing zeros.

position.description: [add_node] Position - {"x","y"} for 2D nodes, {"x","y","z"} for 3D. Shorthand for properties.position

rotation.description: [add_node] Rotation in radians on a 2D node - shorthand for properties.rotation. A 3D node takes {"x","y","z"} under properties.rotation

scale.description: [add_node] Scale - {"x","y"} for 2D nodes, {"x","y","z"} for 3D. Shorthand for properties.scale

texturePath.description: [load_sprite] Texture file path relative to project

newPath.description: [save] Save to a different path instead of overwriting

abortOnError.description: Stop processing on first error (default: false)

tools.name: create_resource
tools.description: Create a .tres resource file from an engine Resource class or a GDScript resource script (class_name or path), with property values set. Values are checked against declared types as in set_node_properties (Property Values in docs/tools.md). Refuses an existing file unless overwrite is true. Returns: resourcePath, resourceType, scriptPath and properties read back from the saved file. Errors on an unknown type or property, and while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

resourcePath.description: Path of the .tres file inside the project, e.g. "items/sword.tres". Created with its folders.

type.description: Engine Resource class such as "StyleBoxFlat", a registered class_name, or a GDScript path such as "items/item_stats.gd". A class_name is known only after the editor or an import has scanned the project.

properties.description: Property values to set, keyed by property name as written, with the same value rules as set_node_properties. script and resource_path are refused.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at resourcePath (default: false).

tools.name: set_resource_properties
tools.description: Set property values in an existing .tres resource file and save it. Properties not named, sub-resources and uids stay as the file has them. A Dictionary or Array value replaces the stored one whole; send every key. Values are checked against declared types as in set_node_properties (Property Values in docs/tools.md); one invalid name or value errors and writes nothing. Returns: resourcePath, resourceType, scriptPath, the named properties read back. Errors while a runtime session is live.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

resourcePath.description: Path of the .tres file inside the project, e.g. "items/sword.tres".

properties.description: Property values to set, at least one, keyed by property name as written, with the same value rules as set_node_properties. script and resource_path are refused.

tools.name: delete_nodes
tools.description: Remove one or more nodes, with their descendants, from a scene. Always-array: pass a single-element nodePaths array for a one-off delete. Saves once at the end. The scene root, a node inside an instanced scene, and a node inherited from a base scene cannot be deleted: that entry reports an error and the rest still process. Returns: results[], one entry per nodePath in input order, each with success or error. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project (e.g. "scenes/main.tscn")

nodePaths.description: Node paths from scene root to delete (e.g. ["root/Player/Sprite2D"])

tools.name: set_node_properties
tools.description: Set node properties in a scene in one Godot process. Always-array: one update for a one-off edit. Each value is checked against the property's declared type, never stored as a zero (Property Values in docs/tools.md). A Dictionary or Array value replaces the stored one whole; send every key. Saves once. Returns: results[], one per update in input order, each with success, error or skipped; warnings leads when a value is set but not saved. Errors while a runtime session is live.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

property.description: GDScript property name in snake_case (e.g. "position", "modulate", "collision_layer"), or "metadata/<name>", or a slash key the node declares (e.g. "theme_override_colors/font_color")

value.description: New property value. Vector2/Vector3/Color auto-convert from {"x","y"} / {"x","y","z"} / {"r","g","b","a"} objects; primitives pass through. Packed*Array and script-declared Array[T] properties take a plain array and the element conversions apply per element (e.g. [{"x":10,"y":20}, ...] for Polygon2D.polygon); a script-declared Dictionary[K, V] takes a plain object (keys are strings, converted to K); an element that cannot represent the element type errors with its index or key instead of silently storing zeros. Object-typed properties (e.g. CollisionShape2D.shape) take a res:// path, a {type: ClassName, ...props} dict that builds a Resource inline, or null to clear; slash-suffixed keys like shader_parameter/<uniform> go inside that dict, not on the node.

abortOnError.description: Stop processing on first error (default: false)

tools.name: get_node_properties
tools.description: Read the current property values of one or more nodes from a scene file, in one Godot process. Always-array: pass a one-element nodes array for one node. Per-node changedOnly: true leaves out properties that match the class defaults. Returns: results[] in input order: { nodePath, nodeType, properties }, or { nodePath, error } when not found. Values use the input shapes of set_node_properties. warnings leads when changedOnly had no defaults to compare. Errors if the scene cannot be loaded.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

changedOnly.description: Only return properties differing from defaults (default: false)

tools.name: attach_script
tools.description: Attach a GDScript or C# script to a node in a scene, replacing any script it had. Check the script with the validate tool first. C# needs the Godot .NET build with the class compiled into the project assembly. Saves automatically. Returns: nodePath and scriptPath. Errors if the script cannot be instantiated (parse errors, @abstract, or an unbuilt C# class), or if scriptPath or nodePath does not exist. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

scriptPath.description: Path to the script file relative to the project (e.g. "scripts/player.gd" or "scripts/Player.cs"). A .cs file needs the Godot .NET build and its class compiled into the project assembly (dotnet build).

tools.name: get_scene_tree
tools.description: Get a scene's node hierarchy as a nested tree. maxDepth: 1 lists only direct children; the default -1 is the whole tree. parentPath scopes to one subtree. Returns: the root node { name, type, path, script, children[] }, every child the same shape; path is a root/... node path the node tools accept, script a res:// path or an empty string. A node cut by maxDepth has children null and a childCount, and warnings leads. Errors if the scene or parentPath is not found.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

parentPath.description: Scope to a subtree starting at this node path (e.g. "root/Player")

maxDepth.description: Maximum recursion depth. -1 for unlimited (default: -1). 1 returns only direct children.

tools.name: duplicate_node
tools.description: Duplicate a node and its descendants, instead of rebuilding it with add_node. newName defaults to the original name plus "2"; targetParentPath to the parent of the original. Keeps the saved signal connections like the editor; copySignals false drops them. Saves automatically. Returns: nodePath (copied node), newNodePath (read back). Errors if nodePath or targetParentPath is not found, nodePath is the root, or a runtime session is live.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

nodePath.description: Node path from scene root to duplicate

newName.description: Name for the duplicated node (default: original name + "2")

targetParentPath.description: Parent node path for the duplicate (default: same parent as original)

copySignals.description: Keep the copy's saved signal connections (default true). False drops those from the copy or a node inside it to a node outside the copied subtree; connections within the subtree stay.

tools.name: move_nodes
tools.description: Move nodes to another parent and/or child position in a scene, each subtree kept whole (owners, groups, connections). Always-array moves, applied in order. Saves once at the end. Returns: results[] per move with success, newNodePath and index read back, or error; warnings leads when a NodePath value no longer leads where it did. Refused per entry: the root, a node inside an instance or inherited, a target inside the node, a name taken at the target. Errors while a runtime session is live.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

moves.description: Moves to apply in order. Each names a node and gives newParentPath, index or both.

nodePath.description: Node path from scene root to move

newParentPath.description: Node path of the new parent ("root" for the scene root; an empty string is an error). Omit to keep the current parent and only reorder. The node keeps its name; a child of that name already there is an error.

index.description: Position among the parent children after the move, 0 = first, -1 = last. Omit to append when the parent changes, or to leave the order when it does not.

tools.name: get_node_signals
tools.description: List all signals defined on a node and their current connections. Use before connect_signal/disconnect_signal to verify signal/method names. The connections[].target field is already scene-root-relative in the "root/..." form connect_signal/disconnect_signal accept as targetNodePath (a self-connection reports as "root") - pass it straight through with no conversion. Returns: nodeType and signals[], each with name and current connections (signal/target/method). Errors if node not found.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

tools.name: connect_signal
tools.description: Connect a signal on a source node to a method on a target node and persist it in the .tscn. Use get_node_signals first to confirm the names. Saves automatically. Returns: nodePath, signal, targetNodePath, method and connected, which is read back from the saved scene (null with a leading warning if that read failed). Errors if the signal or method does not exist or the connection already exists. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

nodePath.description: Source node path from scene root

signal.description: Signal name on the source node (e.g. "pressed", "body_entered")

targetNodePath.description: Target node path from scene root that receives the signal

method.description: Method name on the target node to call when the signal fires

tools.name: disconnect_signal
tools.description: Remove a signal connection between two nodes and persist the change in the .tscn. Use get_node_signals first to confirm the connection exists; connect_signal puts it back. Saves automatically. Returns: nodePath, signal, targetNodePath, method and connected, read back from the saved scene: false once the connection is gone, null with a leading warning if that read failed. Errors if the connection does not exist. Errors while a runtime session is live on this project.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scenePath.description: Scene file path relative to the project

nodePath.description: Source node path from scene root

signal.description: Signal name on the source node

targetNodePath.description: Target node path from scene root

method.description: Method name on the target node

tools.name: profile_project
tools.description: Profile a window: GDScript function costs, fps, monitors; visual adds CPU/GPU ms per render stage, timeline both over time. Requires run_project with profiling: true. Blocks for `seconds` (default 5, max 30; longer: start_profiler). Times are elapsed, not CPU; never sum totalMs (rows overlap). Returns: warnings first, projectPath, complete, fps, slowFrames, rows, frame, servers, worstFrame, monitors, visual, timeline. Errors if profiling is off, a capture is open or the game exits mid-window.

seconds.description: Capture duration in seconds, greater than 0 and at most 30 (default: 5). The call answers only when the window has closed, and with its waits can take up to 58 s, which the limit keeps under a client's 60 s request timeout. Time spent waiting for the session queue counts against that: a call whose wait plus its worst case would pass 60 s is refused with nothing sent. For a longer capture use start_profiler (up to 60 s) and stop_profiler.

top.description: How many functions to return, 1..100 (default: 20). Also caps visual.areas when the capture recorded render stages.

sort.description: Rank by own time ("selfMs", default), inclusive time ("totalMs"), or invocation count ("calls").

captureLimit.description: Rows the engine puts in each frame packet, 16..512 (default: 512). Godot selects them by inclusive time, so a lower limit hides cheap functions and sets limitReached.

visual.description: Also record the editor's Visual Profiler: CPU and GPU milliseconds per render stage (culling, shadows, opaque pass, canvas, ...) in `visual` (default: false). GPU times are null on GLES/web builds of the Compatibility renderer, which time no GPU work; `visual.gpuTimed` is false and a warning says so. A frame holds 256 render markers by default; a scene that needs more makes the engine log an error per lost marker, slowing the game, so the capture switches visual off and its warnings say how to raise the limit.

timeline.description: Also record the capture over time in `timeline.buckets`: per interval the fps, frameMs avg/max, process/physics/script ms, slowFrames, draw calls, render CPU/GPU ms (with visual) and the heaviest functions, server calls or render stages (`top`, named once in `timeline.items`) - where and when frames got slow (default: false). timelineMs, timelineTop, timelineBuckets and track turn it on by themselves; false beside any is rejected.

timelineMs.description: Timeline interval in milliseconds, 250..5000 (default: 500). Records at most about 60 intervals (60 s: 1000 ms) and the reply merges them down to timelineBuckets. Implies timeline.

timelineTop.description: Heaviest functions, server calls or render stages listed per timeline interval, 0..10 (default: 3). 0 leaves `top` empty. Implies timeline.

timelineBuckets.description: Most intervals the timeline reply holds, 4..60 (default: 20). A capture recorded in more is merged: adjacent intervals combine (counts and times add up, maxima stay) and `timeline.bucketMs` reports the width. Implies timeline.

targetFps.description: Frame rate to hold the game to (default: 60). slowFrames counts frames whose frameMs exceeds 1000/targetFps, over the capture and per timeline interval. Under vsync every frame lasts the refresh interval: disable vsync, or set targetFps a few percent below the refresh rate.

track.description: Up to 4 NodePath:property values the game samples during the capture (every 250 ms, or half the interval when shorter), placed on the timeline by frame number, e.g. "/root/Main/Player:global_position" - where the player was when frames got slow. Implies timeline. Uses the bridge: drive the game between start_profiler and stop_profiler, not in parallel with profile_project. Collected only while the session that started the capture is current.

tools.name: start_profiler
tools.description: Start a profiler capture and return at once, so simulate_input, run_script and screenshots drive the game while it records; timeline and track show where frames drop. Requires run_project with profiling: true. Stops itself after `seconds` (default 30, max 60); read it with stop_profiler. Unattended window: use profile_project. Returns: warnings if any, projectPath, active, visual, timeline, timelineMs, firstFrame, captureLimit, maxSeconds. Errors if a capture is running or profiling was off.

seconds.description: Maximum capture duration before the automatic stop, greater than 0 and at most 60 (default: 30).

captureLimit.description: Rows the engine puts in each frame packet, 16..512 (default: 512). Godot selects them by inclusive time, so a lower limit hides cheap functions and sets limitReached.

visual.description: Also record the editor's Visual Profiler: CPU and GPU milliseconds per render stage (culling, shadows, opaque pass, canvas, ...) in `visual` (default: false). GPU times are null on GLES/web builds of the Compatibility renderer, which time no GPU work; `visual.gpuTimed` is false and a warning says so. A frame holds 256 render markers by default; a scene that needs more makes the engine log an error per lost marker, slowing the game, so the capture switches visual off and its warnings say how to raise the limit.

timeline.description: Also record the capture over time in `timeline.buckets`: per interval the fps, frameMs avg/max, process/physics/script ms, slowFrames, draw calls, render CPU/GPU ms (with visual) and the heaviest functions, server calls or render stages (`top`, named once in `timeline.items`) - where and when frames got slow (default: false). timelineMs, timelineTop, timelineBuckets and track turn it on by themselves; false beside any is rejected.

timelineMs.description: Timeline interval in milliseconds, 250..5000 (default: 500). Records at most about 60 intervals (60 s: 1000 ms) and the reply merges them down to timelineBuckets. Implies timeline.

timelineTop.description: Heaviest functions, server calls or render stages listed per timeline interval, 0..10 (default: 3). 0 leaves `top` empty. Implies timeline.

timelineBuckets.description: Most intervals the timeline reply holds, 4..60 (default: 20). A capture recorded in more is merged: adjacent intervals combine (counts and times add up, maxima stay) and `timeline.bucketMs` reports the width. Implies timeline.

targetFps.description: Frame rate to hold the game to (default: 60). slowFrames counts frames whose frameMs exceeds 1000/targetFps, over the capture and per timeline interval. Under vsync every frame lasts the refresh interval: disable vsync, or set targetFps a few percent below the refresh rate.

track.description: Up to 4 NodePath:property values the game samples during the capture (every 250 ms, or half the interval when shorter), placed on the timeline by frame number, e.g. "/root/Main/Player:global_position" - where the player was when frames got slow. Implies timeline. Uses the bridge: drive the game between start_profiler and stop_profiler, not in parallel with profile_project. Collected only while the session that started the capture is current.

tools.name: stop_profiler
tools.description: Stop the start_profiler capture of the current session and rank what it recorded; one that hit its time limit is read back as-is, re-readable with another sort. Times are elapsed, not CPU; inclusive rows overlap, never sum totalMs. Returns: the profile_project payload: warnings first, projectPath, complete (false if cut short), fps, slowFrames, rows, frame, servers, worstFrame, monitors, plus visual and timeline when started with them. Errors if no capture was started.

top.description: How many functions to return, 1..100 (default: 20). Also caps visual.areas when the capture recorded render stages.

sort.description: Rank by own time ("selfMs", default), inclusive time ("totalMs"), or invocation count ("calls").

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Validate GDScript syntax or scene integrity in headless Godot. Use before attach_script or run_script. Give exactly one of scriptPath, source or scenePath, or a targets array (one process); an unknown key is an error. checks needs scenePath and instantiates the scene, running each attached script's _init(). Returns: { warnings?, valid, errors } for one target, { warnings?, results: [{ target, valid, errors }] } for targets; an invalid result always has an error.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scriptPath.description: [single] Path to a .gd file relative to the project to validate (e.g. "scripts/player.gd"). A file that does not load as a GDScript is reported invalid with a "Not validated" error, since nothing checks it.

source.description: [single] Inline GDScript source code to validate. Written to a temporary file and validated against the project.

scenePath.description: [single] Path to a .tscn scene file relative to the project to validate (e.g. "scenes/main.tscn")

checks.description: [single, requires scenePath] Structural and signal-verification checks to run against the scene. Types: "structure" (validate node tree against a schema) and "signals" (verify signal connections and handler methods, optional nodePath scope). Merged into the errors array with a "check" discriminator. Not accepted alongside targets: put checks on the target they belong to.

type.description: The kind of check to run

schema.description: [structure] Recursive node schema: { type?: string, children?: Schema[], hasProperty?: string }. Checks the root node and subtree.

nodePath.description: [signals] Optional node path to scope the check to a subtree (e.g. "root/HUD")

targets.description: [batch] Array of targets to validate in a single Godot process. Each item is an object with exactly one of scriptPath, source or scenePath, or a bare path string (.gd = scriptPath, .tscn or .scn = scenePath). Cannot be combined with the top-level scriptPath, source, scenePath or checks.

scriptPath.description: Path to a .gd file relative to the project

scenePath.description: Path to a .tscn scene file relative to the project

checks.description: [requires scenePath] Structural / signal checks for this target, run in the same Godot process as the rest of the batch. Same shape as the top-level checks array.

type.description: The kind of check to run

schema.description: [structure] Recursive node schema: { type?: string, children?: Schema[], hasProperty?: string }. Checks the root node and subtree.

nodePath.description: [signals] Optional node path to scope the check to a subtree (e.g. "root/HUD")

instructions:
Godot MCP Server - AI-driven Godot 4.5+ project manipulation.

Tool categories:
- Project management: launch_editor, run_project, switch_project, stop_project, get_debug_output, list_projects, check_project
- Scene editing (headless): create_scene, add_node, load_sprite, save_scene, export_mesh_library, batch_scene_operations
- Node editing (headless): delete_nodes, set_node_properties, get_node_properties, attach_script, get_scene_tree, duplicate_node, move_nodes, get_node_signals, connect_signal, disconnect_signal
- Resource files (headless): create_resource, set_resource_properties
- Runtime (requires run_project): take_screenshot, simulate_input, get_ui_elements, run_script
- Render check (no runtime session): render_movie
- Profiling (requires run_project with profiling: true): profile_project, start_profiler, stop_profiler
- Project config (no Godot process): list_autoloads, add_autoload, remove_autoload, update_autoload, get_project_files, search_project, get_scene_dependencies, get_project_settings, set_project_setting
- Validation: validate

Key behaviors:
- All mutation operations (add_node, set_node_properties, delete_nodes, etc.) save the scene automatically. Only use save_scene for save-as (newPath) or re-canonicalization.
- Headless Godot loads every registered autoload. An autoload that stops the engine before the operation is dispatched (for example one that quits in _init) fails every headless operation; one that only errors in _ready does not. Check the script with validate, and use list_autoloads / remove_autoload to find and remove it.
- run_project waits for the MCP bridge before returning success and returns a JSON payload (sessionMode, bridgePort, warnings). If the bridge never answers it returns an error and tears the session down; retry run_project.
- run_project with attach: true is the path for a Godot process you launch yourself: it injects the bridge and marks the project active, but spawns nothing and captures no stdout/stderr. It asks no launch confirmation; run_script still asks once per project. stop_project ends it without killing that process.
- Several projects can run at once, one session per project. run_project on another project adds a session and makes it current; it does not stop the others. The runtime tools, the profiling tools, get_debug_output and stop_project act on the current session only, and every response names it in projectPath. switch_project({ projectPath }) changes which session is current. stop_project stops the current session and leaves none current. When no session is current, or the current one's game has exited, these tools return an error listing the live sessions instead of picking one: call switch_project. check_project reports the current project and every live session.
- A runtime session runs one operation at a time. A runtime, profiling or session call issued while another is still running waits for it (up to 30 s) and then returns an error naming the operation it waited behind; nothing was sent for it, so retry once that operation has returned.
- A runtime session ends by itself when the game exits or an attached bridge disconnects: the bridge autoload is removed at that moment and the scene-editing tools unblock. After a spawned game exits, stop_project is still worth calling (it frees the retained process slot and returns the captured logs) and succeeds. After an attached session ends by itself nothing is left to stop: stop_project then reports no active session, which needs no follow-up.
- click_element in simulate_input resolves by node path or node name (BFS search), NOT by visible text. Use get_ui_elements to discover valid element identifiers.
- simulate_input reports per-action results (signals fired, the Control hit, UI changes, watched values), so it needs no take_screenshot round trip to tell whether an action landed. Omitting `pressed` taps; set it only to hold or release across actions.
- render_movie is a separate short Godot run under the movie writer, with no bridge and no input: use it to check that a scene renders (likelyBlank) or animates (anyMotion) without starting a session. It needs a display, asks for the same launch confirmation as run_project, and is refused while a runtime session is live on the same project.
- run_script expects GDScript with "extends RefCounted" and "func execute(scene_tree: SceneTree) -> Variant".
- run_project spawns Godot without -d so runtime errors do not pause execution; the `breakpoint` keyword in user code is a no-op (no debugger is attached). SCRIPT ERROR output and GDScript backtraces still appear in stderr.
- profiling: true attaches Godot's own remote debugger for the profiling tools. Errors and `breakpoint` still do not pause the game - the server answers every debugger break with continue.
- Every capture reports fps and engine monitors (draw calls, memory, node counts); pass visual: true to profile_project or start_profiler for CPU/GPU time per render stage, and timeline: true (with track: ["/root/Main/Player:global_position"]) to see when and where frames got slow. To capture while simulate_input walks the game, call start_profiler, then simulate_input, then stop_profiler: profile_project holds the session for its whole window, so no other runtime call runs inside it.

Confirmation prompts: the first run_project (spawn mode) or render_movie on a project in a server session asks the user to confirm, because the project's code runs with the user's permissions. The first run_script on a project asks too, because agent-written GDScript runs with those permissions; a launch confirmation does not cover it, and an attached session asks as well. Each prompt is asked once per project per server session, and nothing is scanned. If the user declines, do not call the tool again on that project unless they ask. GODOT_MCP_DISABLE_ELICITATION=true skips the prompts for clients that cannot display them. See SECURITY.md.
